D.t: Mark Warner leads by 19.7 in the forecast and wins 100% of simulations. The cushion is about 731,139 votes; a one point swing is about 18,547 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +12.6 and D +27.0. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Fairfax County, a projected net 248,595 votes; Arlington County, a projected net 76,234 votes; Richmond city, a projected net 71,550 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.

The large counties within 12 points: Spotsylvania County, D +3.0, 1.7% of the vote; Roanoke County, R +8.1, 1.2% of the vote; Fauquier County, R +7.6, 0.9% of the vote; York County, D +2.2, 0.9% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Mark Warner runs furthest behind in Richmond city, Suffolk city, Albemarle County. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 71% of voters, 52 to 45, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.56 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 66% of voters, 58 to 39, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.29 points; Incomes $50K to $124K, 55% of voters, 58 to 39, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.75 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Mark Warner: Immigration voters 22 to 75, Small counties 43 to 54, White voters 52 to 45. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$7.5M cash against $230K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.4 points away from Mark Warner. Election Day has to make it up: the remaining vote must break harder your way than the forecast expects.
